summary: This bill directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish a competition with a cash prize to accelerate the integration of passive anti-drunk driving technology into vehicles, create a Traffic Safety Enforcement Center of Excellence, and establish a national data collection system for drug-involved crashes.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes appropriations from the Highway Trust Fund for a prize competition ($50 million), the establishment of a Traffic Safety Enforcement Center of Excellence ($5 million annually), and a national drug-involved crash data collection system ($30 million annually for several years). These provisions directly increase government spending.

The bill authorizes $50 million from the Highway Trust Fund for a technology prize competition plus $5 million annually for a new enforcement center and $30 million annually for a crash data system, with no offsetting revenue increases or spending reductions. This new mandatory-style spending without offsets would modestly increase the deficit, but the topic is entirely peripheral to the bill's core purpose of advancing drunk-driving prevention technology and enforcement.
